Implement the beat clock module (`src/utils/beat.ts`)

## Summary
Create a new pure, unit-testable beat clock module that derives a beat period from a configurable BPM (default 80 BPM → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes quantisation helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — Module at `src/utils/beat.ts` exposes `beatPeriodMs` (derived from configurable BPM, default 80), `nextTick(elapsedTime, interval)`, and `shotTimeFor(currentTime, interval)` helpers.
- [ ] **AC2** — All helpers are pure and deterministic given an input time — no `Date` or frame coupling.
- [ ] **AC3** — The beat anchor is configurable (defaults to 0/scene start) and advances with game time (pauses with the game).
- [ ] **AC4** — Unit tests cover: period from BPM, quantisation boundaries/edge cases, config override changing cadence.
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert that `nextTick(t, interval)` returns the smallest multiple of `interval` at/after `t`, and `shotTimeFor` snaps to the correct grid tick.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC1** — [ ] **AC1 — Pure, configurable 80 BPM beat clock.** A new pure, unit-testable module (e.g. `src/utils/beat.ts`) derives the beat period from a **configurable** BPM (default **80 BPM** → 750 ms/beat), tracks a beat anchor/time origin, and exposes a quantisation helper that maps an arbitrary elapsed time to the next beat/subdivision tick (`nextTick(t)`, `isOnBeat/fireTimeFor(interval, t)`, etc.). No `Date`/frame coupling; deterministic given an input time.

## Constraints
- No audio or visual beat indicators — silent internal scheduling only.
- Must work with Phasers delta-time model (ms-based).
- Default BPM: 80 (beat period: 750 ms). All per-weapon intervals are exact subdivisions.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/beat.ts` — **NEW** — pure beat clock module.
- `src/utils/beat.test.ts` — **NEW** — unit tests.

## Risks
- Minimal: the module is pure and self-contained. Edge cases: large dt values (frame drops), zero elapsed time.

# Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

## Context

The runtime auto-sequencer (AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X) is fully implemented but not wired into the game. There is no way for designers or testers to interact with it visually. This work item creates a gym scene that provides a hands-on interface for designing and previewing difficulty curves.

discovered-from:AH-0MUDIWETP003XC3X

## Goal

Add a new **Dev Utilities** category/section to the gym index, and create a gym scene within it that provides:

1. **Curve editor** — an interactive way to define the target difficulty curve (array of scores, one per wave)
2. **Regenerate button** — when clicked, runs the sequencer against the current curve and displays the resulting waves
3. **Wave list** — shows each generated wave with its enemy composition, target difficulty, and the resulting wave
4. **Edit-to-clear behaviour** — if the curve is edited, the wave list is cleared and replaced with an instruction to click the regenerate button

## Scope

- Add a **Dev Utilities** column/section to the gym index (GymIndex.ts) — follows the same pattern as the existing ENEMIES and Bosses columns
- Create src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts (and its test file)
- The scene uses the existing sequencer() from difficultySequencer.ts
- Plain-DOM tuning panel overlay (same pattern as GymPlayer) for the curve editor
- Phaser canvas for the wave list display (Phaser text objects)

## Curve editor design

- Each wave in the curve is represented as a row with:
  - A numeric slider (0–100) for the target difficulty
  - A Remove button to delete that wave row
- An "Add Wave" button to append a new wave row at the end
- The "Regenerate" button runs the sequencer and populates the wave list below
- When the curve is edited (any slider moved, wave added/removed), the wave list is cleared and replaced with instruction text: "Edit made — click Regenerate to preview"

## Wave list display

- Each wave entry shows:
  - Wave number
  - Target difficulty
  - Enemy composition (enemy type, count)
  - Whether shooting is enabled
- Entries rendered as Phaser text objects, ordered top-to-bottom

## Non-goals

- Saving/loading curves (could be added later)
- Visual preview of enemy formations (text-only for now)
- Drag-to-reorder waves in the curve editor

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Gym index shows a "Dev Utilities" section** — a new column or section in the gym index listing gym scenes under the Dev Utilities category
2. **GymCurveSequencer scene is listed** under the Dev Utilities section and can be launched from the gym index
3. **Curve editor works** — user can add wave rows, remove wave rows, and adjust target difficulty via sliders (0–100)
4. **Regenerate button** — clicking it runs sequencer() with the current curve and candidate pool, populating the wave list
5. **Wave list is cleared on curve edit** — when the user edits the curve (any change), the wave list is replaced with instruction text to click regenerate
6. **Wave entries display correctly** — each shows wave number, target difficulty, enemy composition, and shooting status
7. **Back to index button** works (arrow-left INDEX)
8. **ESC returns to main menu** (consistent with other gym scenes)
9. **All tests pass** — the scene has unit tests verifying the curve editor and regenerate flow

## Revision — audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the first implementation with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. Make the wave description a table, with column headings. Provide a help box in the bottom right summarizing each column.

Additional acceptance criteria:

10. **Wave preview is a table** — the wave preview renders a table with column headings (Wave, Target, Composition, Shooting) and one aligned row per wave.
11. **Column guide help box** — a help box anchored to the bottom-right of the canvas summarises each wave-table column.

## Revision — second audit follow-up (2026-09-27)

Manual review rejected the implementation again with the following note:

> Rejected by manual review. The UI works, but the generated levels are not good. Firstly, why do we have an actual and error value? Why don't we just create as close the target as possible? Secondly, the higher levels seem to just repeat the phaser with shooting.

Root cause confirmed by reproducing the sequencer output: `sequencer()` picked exactly one candidate group per wave and a single group's `enemyDifficulty` score saturates around 33 (e.g. `phaser×12`), so every target at or above ~40 produced the identical `phaser×12` wave — hence the large error values and the repetition.

Revised acceptance criteria:

12. **Wave generation reaches the target** — the preview table no longer shows redundant ACTUAL/ERROR columns; the table columns are WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING. The sequencer composes a wave from one or more candidate groups so the wave's summed difficulty is within a small tolerance of the target for every target above the old single-group ceiling (previously capped at ~33) up to 100.
13. **Higher waves are varied** — waves with different (especially higher) targets produce meaningfully different enemy compositions instead of every high wave repeating the same archetype (e.g. `phaser` with shooting).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/GymIndex.ts — add Dev Utilities section
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts — new scene
- src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.test.ts — tests for the scene
- src/core/difficultySequencer.ts — sequencer (extended to compose multi-group waves)
- src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts — existing scorer (read-only)
- src/core/enemyConfig.ts — existing enemy configs for candidate pool
- src/utils/gymNavigation.ts — shared back-to-index navigation
- src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts — gym scene auto-discovery (no changes needed, scene auto-appears)
data.title: Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview

# Goal

Fix the audit runner's parent-first flow so that child `partial` verdicts caused by unserviced in-main-slot items are treated as "not assessed" rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision, and add diagnostic clarity.

# Background

In `--child-in-main-slot` mode (default), child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking agent session. In non-interactive runs (e.g. downtime workers), these items are never serviced, leaving all child AC verdicts as `partial`.

Currently, `_build_issue_json` treats ALL `partial` verdicts as unacceptable, causing the parent to report "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met, because the child partials (from unserviced in-main-slot work) are counted as failures.

# Implementation Plan

## 1. Track in-main-slot partial verdicts

Add a `verdict_reason` field to child AC results when they are `partial` due to in-main-slot unserviced work. The `_phase1_review_child_acs` and `_deep_analyze_child` functions already set `verdict: "partial"` with evidence like `"pending (main-session review)"` in in-main-slot mode. We need to mark these explicitly with `verdict_reason: "unserviced-in-main-slot"`.

## 2. Handle partials in `_build_issue_json`

Modify `all_ac_acceptable` computation to skip child ACs whose `partial` verdict has `verdict_reason == "unserviced-in-main-slot"`. These should be treated as "not assessed" and NOT block the parent's readiness-to-close decision.

## 3. Add diagnostic output

In the audit summary/JSON output, surface a clear diagnostic that distinguishes:
- Children with `partial` verdicts from unserviced in-main-slot work → "not assessed"
- Children with genuine `partial` or `unmet` verdicts → "not-ready"

Add a `children_assessment` section to the `_build_issue_json` output listing `unserviced_in_main_slot` child IDs and `genuine_not_ready` child IDs.

# Acceptance Criteria
- AC2: Parent audit treats in-main-slot unserviced partials as "not assessed" (does NOT block ready-to-close)
- AC3: Audit output includes diagnostic distinguishing unserviced-in-main-slot partials from genuine failures

# Constraints
- Must not change behaviour of interactive runs (where agent CAN service in-main-slot items)
- Must be backward-compatible with persisted audit results

# Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase1_review_child_acs`, `_deep_analyze_child`, `_build_issue_json`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — existing in-main-slot tests
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness tests (verify no regression)

# Intake brief — Harvester enemy

**Headline:** Add a Harvester enemy archetype — a large, slow, roaming enemy
that actively seeks and absorbs the nearest mineral and survives five player
bullets — backed by data-driven regular-enemy health, wired into both the
shipped game and the enemy gym, and integrated into the campaign as a rare
roaming spawn.

## Problem statement

The bestiary currently has no enemy that competes with the player for
minerals. Non-asteroid enemies already absorb any mineral they happen to
overlap (GDD §4.4.1), but none deliberately hunts the field. The Harvester
introduces a mineral-denial threat: it actively drives to the nearest mineral,
is large (easy to hit and quick to absorb), slow to cross the screen, and
durable (five hits), forcing the player to spend ammunition and attention on it
before it strips the field.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want a durable enemy that actively steals minerals, so
  that collecting minerals becomes a contest rather than a free pickup.
- **As a player**, I want the Harvester to be large and slow, so that the
  five-hit cost is fair and readable rather than punishing.
- **As a designer**, I want to tune the Harvester (size, colour, speed,
  health, score) through the existing CSV/enemy-config pipeline without
  touching scene code.
- **As a developer**, I want multi-hit health and mineral seeking to be shared,
  data-driven capabilities, so future multi-hit or seeking enemies are cheap
  and the game and gyms cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New `harvester` archetype is registered and discoverable.** A
  `harvester` row exists in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` with a matching seed
  fallback in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, is mapped in
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, appears in the gym index, and spawns/renders
  in `GymEnemies`. Regular-enemy health is data-driven: a `health` column is
  added to the CSV schema/codec (`src/core/csv.ts`) and `EnemyConfig`
  (`src/core/configTypes.ts`), defaulting to 1 so existing enemies are
  unchanged. Verified by config/CSV tests and a gym spawn test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Mineral-seeking behaviour.** The Harvester always steers toward
  the **nearest live mineral anywhere on the field** at its configured (slow)
  speed and absorbs it on overlap using the existing enemy-absorption rule
  (`collectMinerals`), incrementing its tracked mineral count. It does **not
  fire**, and it cannot take minerals from the player's hold. When no mineral
  exists it holds station / continues its idle drift. Verified by deterministic
  entity + scene tests that place minerals and assert the Harvester closes
  distance and consumes them, and that it fires no bullets.
- [ ] **AC3 — Five-hit destruction with readable feedback.** The Harvester has
  `health = 5` and survives exactly five player-bullet hits. Each non-lethal hit
  consumes the bullet and triggers the existing bullet-impact feedback; the
  fifth hit destroys it, plays destruction audio/VFX exactly once, awards
  **≈ 400** score, advances wave accounting, and re-drops 25–50 % of absorbed
  minerals per the existing rule. The shared multi-hit path must correctly
  finalise the kill (`onEnemyDestroyed`, destruction audio) — a gap that exists
  today. Verified by a five-hit test and a single-destruction/single-audio
  regression test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Existing enemies are unchanged.** All current 1-HP enemies
  (Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm, Asteroid) remain destroyed by one hit and
  their tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Game ↔ gym parity.** The Harvester's seek, absorption and
  five-hit destruction run through the same shared code path in `PlayScene` and
  in `GymEnemies` (per the gym-parity principle); no scene re-implements the
  behaviour.
- [ ] **AC6 — Campaign integration.** The Harvester is available in the gym
  **and** appears in the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels
  (Levels 4–5), registered with the `WaveManager` so wave-clear accounting is
  correct. Verified by a wave/level test.
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New unit/integration tests cover: config
  codec round-trip (including the new `health` column), factory mapping, seek
  target selection (nearest mineral; none present), absorption counting,
  five-hit destruction, and a `PlayScene` + `GymEnemies` parity check. Full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
  the changes, including the Game Design Document health model and enemy
  catalog (§2.3, §4.1, §4.4.1, §4.5, §6.5), the
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` catalog and add-an-enemy checklist
  (§1/§8), the README enemy list, and code comments.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven:** tuning lives in the CSV/enemy-config pipeline; no new
  per-enemy scene or hard-coded archetype branch.
- **Single source of truth:** no duplication of collision, mineral-collection,
  or health logic — this is a hard requirement of the gym-parity epic
  (`AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`).
- **No regression:** existing 1-HP enemies and their tests must be untouched
  semantically; `health` defaults to 1.
- **GDD consistency:** the health-model change must be documented explicitly so
  the GDD no longer claims "all regular enemies are 1 HP"; P4 Bomb still deals
  **no** damage to enemies.
- **Surgical:** match existing entity/config/scene style; do not delete
  unrelated dead code (report it instead).
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation.
- **Gating:** implementation proceeds only through `/skill:implement`; this
  intake does not authorise code changes.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-27 against HEAD)

- Enemy archetypes are **data, not code**: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`),
  one CSV row per archetype (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`), seed fallbacks in
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, factory mapping in `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`.
- All regular enemies are **1 HP** (destroyed by a single bullet) and the GDD
  states this explicitly (`docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.3, §4.1, §6.5).
  Only the Boss is multi-hit (4-phase). There is an optional `takeDamage?()`
  seam on entities (`CombatCoreScene`, `CombatScene`, `GymFormationScene`), but
  the shared generic path currently calls it **without** running
  `onEnemyDestroyed()`/destruction audio when the entity finally dies — that
  is a gap this work must close for a multi-hit regular enemy to score, drop
  minerals and advance waves correctly.
- The Asteroid is the precedent for a **non-formation roamer**: it has
  `formationKind: single`, overrides `updatePosition(dt)` (called by the gym
  and game before `applyFormationPosition`) and `applyFormationPosition` is a
  no-op. Asteroids use the same random offscreen spawner
  (`src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`) registered with the `WaveManager`.
- Minerals already exist: `Mineral` (`src/entities/Mineral.ts`), collection and
  non-asteroid absorption in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`
  (`collectMinerals`), kill re-drop in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts`,
  and the 25–50 % re-drop fraction in `src/core/rules.ts`. `BaseEnemy` already
  tracks `mineralCount` / `collectMineral()` / `mineralRedropCount()`.
- The shared enemy-fire dispatcher (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`) already
  mentions the "planned Harvester" as the example of a one-line wiring change.

## Desired change

1. Generalise enemy health data-driven: add a `health` CSV column + codec +
   `EnemyConfig.health` (default 1), and make the shared collision path
   correctly finalise a multi-hit kill (audio, `onEnemyDestroyed`, drops, wave
   accounting).
2. Add a `Harvester` entity (`health = 5`) that roams (like the Asteroid) and
   steers toward the nearest live mineral, absorbing it on overlap; no firing.
3. Register the archetype (CSV + seed + factory + score ≈ 400) and expose it in
   the gym.
4. Integrate it into the campaign as a rare roaming spawn in later levels,
   registered with the `WaveManager`.
5. Update the GDD/ENEMY design docs/README for the health-model and enemy
   catalog changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — New `harvester` row (`health = 5`); add a
  `health` column to every row (default 1).
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — `health` field on `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — `health` column in `ENEMY_COLUMN_ORDER`, coercion and
  validation.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — `harvester` seed fallback (+ default health 1
  for existing seeds).
- `src/entities/Harvester.ts` — New roamer entity: slow seek movement, large
  body, five-hit health, no firing.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Shared multi-hit health / `takeDamage`
  behaviour (or a small shared health helper).
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Map `harvester` → `Harvester`.
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` — No-firing archetype handling (the Harvester
  must not fall back to the aimed shot).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — Finalise a multi-hit kill through
  `onEnemyDestroyed` + destruction audio; supply the live mineral field to
  seeking entities.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Wire seeking/minerals, score value, roamer
  movement, wave/score accounting.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` —
  Expose the same mineral list/seek seam and multi-hit path.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` / `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` /
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — Campaign roaming-spawn integration.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SCORE_VALUES.harvester` ≈ 400.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — Documentation updates.
- Tests: `src/entities/Harvester.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`,
  `src/core/enemyConfig.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` — Gym↔game behavioural-parity epic (critical, open).
  This work must consume the shared cores it establishes and must not add a new
  divergence.
- `AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46` — Shared enemy-fire dispatch (completed). Names the
  Harvester as the exemplar of one-line fire wiring.
- `AH-0MUII3DHM008L7JF` — Shared mineral layer: collection, hold/overflow,
  choice overlay (completed).
- `AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB` — Gym asteroids do not drop minerals / shared
  kill-drop rule (open); relevant to the re-drop path.
- `AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F` — E6 Asteroid non-formation roamer (completed).
  Precedent architecture for a roaming enemy.
- `AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR` — Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in
  GDD (completed). The GDD's 1-HP rule is revised by this work (see Resolved
  decisions).
- `AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K` — Enemy difficulty scoring (completed). Health is not
  currently a scored factor.
- `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT` — Add a health factor to the enemy difficulty index
  (created, low priority, `discovered-from:AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2`). Tracks the
  difficulty-scoring follow-up so it does not creep into this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — multi-hit kill does not finalise.** The current
  `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` `takeDamage` branch skips `onEnemyDestroyed` and
  destruction audio. Mitigation: extend the shared seam and pin it with a test
  so score/wave/drop/audio happen exactly once on the killing blow.
- **Risk — seek seam duplication.** Giving the entity the mineral list must be
  done once in the shared collision/tick path, not copied into each scene
  (parity epic). Mitigation: add a single `setSeekTargets`/equivalent seam
  alongside the existing `setAimTarget`.
- **Risk — health-model regression.** Generalising health could accidentally
  weaken the one-hit guarantee for existing enemies. Mitigation: `health`
  defaults to 1 and a regression test asserts one-hit destruction for every
  existing archetype.
- **Risk — difficulty under-scoring.** `enemyDifficulty` has no health factor.
  Mitigation: tracked separately as `AH-0MUJPTR7Q0070BDT`.
- **Risk — scope creep into wave/level design.** Wiring a new roamer into the
  campaign can balloon. Mitigation: scope is a rare roaming spawn in Levels 4–5
  only; the gym demonstration is the tuning surface.
- **Assumption — "collects it" reuses existing absorption.** The Harvester
  absorbs the mineral on overlap and tallies it; on death it re-drops 25–50 %
  per the existing rule.
- **Assumption — no dedicated health bar.** Feedback for non-lethal hits is the
  existing bullet-impact VFX (plus bullet consumption) rather than a drawn
  health bar; the producer's Q1 sub-question was not separately answered, so
  this minimal readable feedback is the default and can be revisited.
- **Assumption — tuning values are implementation/gym choices.** "Large" and
  "slow" are the requirements; exact px size/speed/colour are chosen and tuned
  in the gym (indicative: size ≈ 40–48 px, speed ≈ 20–30 px/s).
- **Assumption — the Harvester does not fire.**

## Resolved decisions (producer, 2026-09-27)

1. **Health model — data-driven.** Add a `health` column to the enemy-config
   pipeline and generalise multi-hit destruction for regular enemies; update the
   GDD. P4 Bomb continues to deal no damage to enemies. No dedicated health bar
   (minimal impact feedback); see Assumptions.
2. **Mineral-seeking semantics — literal seek.** Always seek the nearest live

# Intake Brief — When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion (AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC)

## Headline

Add a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" SFX to the wave-timeout path,
played once per detonating ship (with a concurrency/rate limiter), so the 10×
detonation of surviving enemies is no longer silent.

## Problem statement

When a wave times out, every surviving non-asteroid enemy detonates at 10×
scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), but no explosion sound plays for those
detonations. The only audio on the timeout path is the generic player
life-loss cue (`playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`), so the
dramatic 10× visual blast lands silently and the moment reads as flat.

## Users

- **Player** — the wave-timeout wipe should be audible as a major explosion,
  making the lost life and the 10× detonation feel consequential.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — one place (exported constants) to tune
  the cue's layering, volume, duration and voice cap.

### Example user story

- As a **player**, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies
  detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major
  event rather than a silent animation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid
  survivor via `s.entity.destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` and calls
  `_loseLife(false)`; it plays **no SFX for the detonations**.
  `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE = 10`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `destroySelf(scale)` → `playExplosion(scale)`
  only spawns particles; the class comment states audio is played by the scene
  at destruction time.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playDestructionSound()` (generic 440→60 Hz
  sawtooth pop) and the layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (impact thump +
  descending body + noise tail). No "major" or timeout-specific cue exists.
- GDD §7.3 documents the two existing cues and states "the wave-timeout life
  penalty and shield absorption keep the generic cue". It also flags the risk
  "SFX rate limiting — … avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX
  instances".
- Tests live in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`
  and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a new dedicated, layered `playMajorExplosionSound()` cue in
`src/audio/effects.ts` and wire it into `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` so it fires
once per detonating ship, guarded by a concurrency/rate limiter so stacked cues
stay within the GDD §7.3 audio ceiling. Document the new cue in GDD §7.3 and
cover it with automated tests.

## Producer decisions (recorded)

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: B** → one heavy cue **per detonating ship**, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: A** → a **new dedicated** `playMajorExplosionSound()`,
  not a reuse of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: A** → keep the **generic**
  `playDestructionSound()` for the player's timeout life loss; only the enemy
  detonations get the major blast cue.

## Assumptions

1. The limiter caps concurrent major-explosion voices at an exported
   `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` (default aligned to the GDD's "≤ 3–4 concurrent
   SFX" guidance); triggers beyond the cap are coalesced/attenuated rather than
   stacking at full gain. [ASSUMPTION]
2. Scope is audio only — the 10× particle blast already exists, so no new VFX.
   [ASSUMPTION]
3. `PlayScene` is the only wave-timeout path (no gym scene has a wave timeout),
   so wiring is confined to `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`. [ASSUMPTION]
4. The cue routes through the existing SFX master gain/mute plumbing and is a
   safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
   browsers). [ASSUMPTION]

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` is defined in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` using layered procedural synthesis (impact thump +
   descending body + noise tail), with every amplitude, duration and voice-cap
   value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant; the cue is
   documented in GDD §7.3.
2. When a wave/level times out with surviving non-asteroid enemies, the major
   explosion cue is triggered **once per detonating ship** (verified by a
   `PlayScene` test whose spy count equals the number of detonated survivors).
3. A concurrency/rate limiter keeps stacked per-ship cues within the GDD §7.3
   audio ceiling: no more than `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` concurrent
   major-explosion voices, with excess triggers attenuated/coalesced — verified
   by unit tests that exercise many simultaneous triggers.
4. When a wave/level times out with no enemies remaining, no major-explosion
   cue plays and the player's generic life-loss cue is unchanged (no
   `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on this path) — verified by tests.
5. The cue routes through the SFX master volume/mute and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext` — verified by tests.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All SFX remain **procedural** (Web Audio API, zero external audio assets) per
  GDD §7.3.
- Respect the GDD §7.3 ceiling and the "avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent
  SFX instances" risk mitigation.
- No new gameplay behaviour: the timeout detonation/one-life penalty is
  unchanged; this is feedback only.
- No new VFX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playMajorExplosionSound()` and its
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` tuning/limiter constants (mirroring the layered
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` structure).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the new cue once per detonating ship in
  `_timeoutWave()` (alongside `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)`);
  leave `_loseLife(false)` and its generic cue untouched.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Unit tests
  for layering, limiter/voice cap, master volume/mute routing and
  no-AudioContext no-op.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Timeout wiring tests (one cue per ship, none
  when no enemies, generic player cue unchanged).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX event catalog and player audio
  character section: document the new major-explosion cue and its limiter.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Limiter tuning may need an audio playtest.** Whether the per-ship stack
  reads as one "major" blast or as mud cannot be judged from unit tests alone;
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` and per-voice gain are exported for tuning.
  [Medium]
- **Masking/clipping risk.** Many near-simultaneous heavy cues could mask
  other SFX or clip; mitigated by the voice cap/attenuation (GDD §7.3 "avoid
  stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances"). [Medium]
- **Browser autoplay policy.** The cue stays silent until a user gesture
  starts the `AudioContext`; it must remain a safe no-op when no context
  exists. [Low]
- **Scope-creep guard.** Reusing the new major cue for other events (boss
  death, P4 bomb clear, player death) is out of scope; record those as linked
  work items rather than widening this item. [Low]
- **Assumption:** no gym wave-timeout path exists today; if one is added
  later, it must reuse the same cue + limiter rather than duplicating it.
  [Low]

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x
  scale and cost a life (added the timeout detonation; completed).
- AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over (completed).
- AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY — Need juice when the player is destroyed (precedent for

- AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A — dedicated player-destruction cue (implemented
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player

- AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH — Add randomness to explosion (completed).

# Single-formation wave groups can declare more enemies than they spawn

## Problem statement

`WaveManager.waveEnemyCount()` (`_waveSize`) reports a wave's declared size by
summing each group's `count`, but `planGroupSpawns` builds the actual spawn list
from the group's formation builder — and `buildSingleOffset`
(`src/utils/formations.ts`) deliberately ignores its `count` argument and always
returns exactly one offset. A `single`-formation group with `count > 1`
therefore declares more enemies than it spawns, so the alive count seeded by
`beginGame()` (`_waveSize(currentWave())`) exceeds `planSpawns().length`. The
wave-clear invariant (`enemiesAlive` reaches zero only after every planned spawn
is destroyed) then relies on the player destroying enemies that were never
spawned, and any future sequencer/authoring path that emits `count > 1` for a
`single` group can stall or clear a wave early.

## Users

- **Level designer / content author** — hand-authors or retunes level/wave
  definitions (and may later widen sequencer count ranges); needs a wave's
  declared enemy count to match what actually spawns, or an immediate,
  actionable validation error when it cannot.
- **Player** — experiences correct wave pacing: a wave must not stall waiting on
  enemies that never spawned, nor clear while spawned enemies remain.
- **Reviewer / producer** — needs the "declared == planned" invariant pinned by
  a regression test, and the resolution direction (validate vs. account from
  planned spawns) recorded so it stays auditable.

Example user stories:

- *As a level designer, I want a wave's declared enemy count to equal its
  planned spawns, so that wave-clear accounting cannot diverge from what the
  player faces.*
- *As a level designer, I want a clear validation error if I configure a
  `single`-formation group with `count > 1`, so that I can correct the data
  rather than debug a stalled wave.*
- *As a reviewer, I want a regression test pinning the declared-vs-planned
  invariant for the `single` formation, so that the defect cannot silently
  return.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Declared count matches planned spawns (or is rejected).** For any wave
  containing a `single`-formation group, either
  `waveEnemyCount() === planSpawns().length`, or the wave is rejected with a
  clear validation error/message that names the offending group and its
  `count`. The inconsistent state (declared > planned) must not be reachable.
- **AC2 — Regression test pins the invariant.** A unit test asserts the
  declared-vs-planned invariant for a `single`-formation group, including the
  `count > 1` case (either equal counts, or a thrown/returned validation error
  with the expected message). Existing `single` semantics
  (`buildSingleOffset` always returns one centred offset) remain pinned.
- **AC3 — No regression in the built-in campaign or sequencer calibration.**
  `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/core/difficultySequencer.test.ts` and
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts` remain green; any test that
  currently relies on an inconsistent `single` group (e.g. `wave('asteroid',
  'single', 2)`) is updated to a valid configuration rather than left asserting
  the broken behaviour.
- **AC4 — Documentation updated.** In-code comments on `buildSingleOffset` /
  `planGroupSpawns` / `_waveSize` (and the chosen validation/accounting helper)
  state that a `single` group represents exactly one entity and that declared
  and planned counts must agree. `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is
  updated where it describes formation kinds/geometry and wave groups. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Do not change `buildSingleOffset`'s single-entity semantics.** It is
  documented as "Single-entity formation for the Boss" and pinned by
  `src/utils/formations.test.ts` (`buildSingleOffset(99)` and
  `buildSingleOffset(0)` both return `[{ row: 0, col: 0 }]`). The `single`
  formation means one entity; making it emit `count` overlapping offsets would
  contradict the type name, the Boss usage and the existing test.
- **One code path (gym↔game parity).** Formation geometry and wave spawn
  planning stay in the shared core (`src/utils/formations.ts`,
  `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`); no divergent copy in gyms or scenes
  (AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity").
- **Pure and deterministic.** Wave planning/validation must remain free of
  Phaser runtime dependencies so it stays unit-testable
  (`planGroupSpawns` is pure; `WaveManager` is a pure state machine).
- **Preserve the sequencer guard.** The `defaultCandidatePool()` guard added in
  AH-0MUDYTPMC002GLEJ (pinning `single`-formation archetypes to their seed

- **AsteroidSpawner (AH-0MUGCH1L0005HXDG)** and dynamic-spawn registration

- **Filter asteroids in `_timeoutWave()` and re-register them (Phase 1)

# Intake Brief: Asteroids do not need to be cleared for a wave to be completed — AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO

**Priority: High** | **Type: bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> A wave must complete as soon as every non-asteroid (enemy ship) in it is
> destroyed. Asteroids no longer count toward a wave's alive target, and both
> asteroids and minerals persist in place across wave and level transitions.

## Problem Statement

Asteroids are currently registered with the `WaveManager` as dynamic spawns
(`registerDynamicSpawn(1)`) when they are released from the offscreen spawner
and when a large/medium asteroid splits. They therefore inflate the wave's
`enemiesAlive` counter, so a wave cannot complete until **every asteroid —
including every split child — is destroyed** (or the wave timer expires). This
forces players to chase slow, non-firing rocks to advance, and it contradicts
the intended rule that only enemy ships gate wave completion. It also causes
asteroids to be cleared/short-circuited at wave boundaries instead of behaving
like classic-Asteroids debris that lingers in the field.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** completes a wave by destroying the enemy ships, without
  having to sweep the field of drifting asteroids first.
  - *"As a player, I want a wave to complete as soon as the enemy ships are
    gone, so drifting asteroids don't stall my progress through the campaign."*
  - *"As a player, I want asteroids and minerals to persist between waves and
    levels, so the field feels like a continuous classic-Asteroids environment
    rather than resetting every wave."*
- **Developer / maintainer:** the wave-completion rule is expressed in one
  place (`WaveManager` accounting + how `PlayScene` feeds it), so it cannot
  drift between the game and its tests.
- **Tester:** can assert deterministic wave completion with live asteroids
  present, and asteroid/mineral persistence across transitions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Wave completion ignores asteroids.** When all non-asteroid enemies in the
   active wave are destroyed, `WaveManager.onEnemyDestroyed()` returns
   `waveCleared` / `levelCleared` / `bossTriggered` as appropriate **regardless
   of how many asteroids (any tier) remain alive**. Asteroids and asteroid
   split children never increment `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`.
2. **Asteroids persist.** Surviving asteroids remain alive in the scene across
   wave and level transitions, continuing straight-line motion, four-edge
   wrapping, rotation, and remaining shootable (player bullets still destroy
   them and still cascade splits).
3. **Split behaviour preserved (gameplay only).** Destroying a large/medium
   asteroid still spawns exactly two smaller children at its position with
   divergent directions, and the children persist and can be shot; the split no
   longer affects wave accounting (no `registerDynamicSpawn`).
4. **Wave-timeout unchanged for ships.** On wave-timeout, every surviving
   non-asteroid enemy still detonates at 10× scale and costs exactly one life;
   surviving asteroids are **not** re-registered with the `WaveManager` (they no
   longer gate the next wave) and remain alive and persistent.
5. **Minerals persist.** Minerals already on the field remain in place across
   wave and level transitions and remain collectable (player) / absorbable
   (non-asteroid enemies); no new mineral behaviour is introduced.
6. **Boss entry keeps clearing asteroids.** Carried-over asteroids are still
   destroyed when the boss encounter begins (the boss encounter spawns no
   asteroids). This preserves the documented boss-entry behaviour and is
   recorded as an assumption below.
7. **Tests updated and comprehensive.** Unit/integration tests cover: wave
   clears with live asteroids present; `enemiesAlive` excludes asteroids and
   split children; asteroids persist across a wave and a level transition;
   timeout does not re-register asteroids. The existing contradictory tests
   (e.g. `AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed`
   and `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5 — carried-over asteroids are re-registered…`)
   are replaced with tests for the new rule.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, the GDD (§4.1 E6 "Wave placement" and §4.2 wave definition)
   and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the game's wave model.** Only `PlayScene` + `WaveManager` own
  wave completion; the formation gyms (`src/scenes/gym/`) have no `WaveManager`
  and their wipe→respawn cycle is a training construct, so they are out of
  scope. The shared asteroid-split helper (`scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`) is
  unchanged, so game/gym split behaviour stays identical.
- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The split helper and mineral rules stay
  shared; only the wave-accounting call site in `PlayScene` changes. Document
  the reason for the `WaveManager`-only scope in the work item/comment.
- **Do not remove `registerDynamicSpawn` / `unregisterDynamicSpawn`** even if
  they become unused by asteroids; keep them as a general dynamic-spawn seam
  (mention as potentially unused rather than deleting).
- **No new spawner/balance tuning** (spawn cadence, tier weights, asteroid
  count) — those are out of scope.
- **Deterministic tests** only; no wall-clock waits.

## Existing State

- `WaveManager` (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts`) tracks `_enemiesAlive`, seeded from
  the wave's formation groups. `onEnemyDestroyed()` decrements it and emits the
  clear event when it reaches zero. `registerDynamicSpawn(n)` /
  `unregisterDynamicSpawn(n)` adjust it mid-wave.
- `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`) registers every released asteroid
  (`_spawnScheduledAsteroid`) and every split child (`_splitAsteroid`) via
  `registerDynamicSpawn(1)`, and re-registers surviving asteroids after a
  timeout (`_timeoutWave`).
- `PlayScene._clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry()` destroys carried-over asteroids when
  the boss encounter begins.
- Minerals already persist across wave/level transitions (they are only cleared
  on run reset/teardown).
- Docs currently assert the opposite rule: GDD §4.1 E6 ("every spawned child
  counts toward the wave's alive target (dynamic spawn registration in
  `WaveManager`)") and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` ("registered …
  so wave-clear accounting includes it").
- Tests asserting the old rule exist in `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (e.g. `PlayScene.test.ts` AC6 and
  `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`).

## Desired Change

1. Stop registering asteroids (spawned or split) with the `WaveManager`;
   `enemiesAlive` reflects formation/enemy-ship count only.
2. Remove the timeout re-registration of surviving asteroids in `_timeoutWave`.
3. Keep asteroids alive and moving through wave/level transitions (already
   supported by `_moveAsteroids`, `_handleAsteroidCollisions` and the
   `transitioning` branch of `tick`); keep them shootable and splitting.
4. Leave boss-entry clearing (`_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry`) in place.
5. Update the contradicting tests and the two documentation sections.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — drop `registerDynamicSpawn(1)` from
  `_spawnScheduledAsteroid` and `_splitAsteroid`; drop the surviving-asteroid
  re-registration block in `_timeoutWave`; update the related code comments.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — keep the API, but clarify in the doc comment that
  asteroids are not registered; `_enemiesAlive` semantics unchanged.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — update/replace tests that assert asteroids
  gate the wave.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace `AC6` and `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`
  with tests for the new rule; add persistence-across-transition tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E6 (wave placement / registration) and
  §4.2 (wave definition: cleared when enemy ships destroyed; asteroids and
  minerals persist).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — remove the "wave-clear accounting
  includes it" claim; state the persistence rule.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneHUD.test.ts` — check for affected wave-accounting
  assumptions and update if needed.

## Related Work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F — Asteroids as an enemy** (feature, done): introduced
  the asteroid and the split-into-two mechanic.
- **AH-0MU8FOR0H0099EO4 — Wave Manager Dynamic Spawn Registration + Unit Tests**
  (task, done): added `registerDynamicSpawn`/`unregisterDynamicSpawn` and
  explicitly required the wave **not** to clear until all split children die.
  This brief reverses that specific AC.
- **AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over** (bug, done): made asteroids survive timeout and
  re-registered them to gate the next wave — the re-registration is removed
  here (survival/persistence is kept).
- **AH-0MU97GM84007X1OW — Add tests for asteroid survival on wave-timeout
  (Phase 1)** (task, done): its AC5 re-registration assertion is superseded.
- **AH-0MUDYS2SZ004H123 — Asteroids spawn randomly offscreen** (feature, done):
  the offscreen spawner whose releases currently register dynamic spawns.
- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10×
  scale and cost a life** (feature, done): the timeout path being adjusted.
- **AH-0MUCG5TIU000VPVO** — boss-entry clearing of carried-over asteroids
  (kept as-is).

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Test/documentation drift (high likelihood, low impact):** several tests and
  two docs assert the old rule. Mitigation: grep for `registerDynamicSpawn`,
  "dynamic spawn" and "wave-clear accounting" and update every reference in the
  same change (AC7/AC8).
- **Unbounded asteroid accumulation (medium likelihood, medium impact):** because
  asteroids persist and the spawner adds more each wave, a long run can build a
  large drifting field. Mitigation: accepted as the intended classic-Asteroids
  behaviour; no cap in scope. If play-testing shows performance or difficulty
  degradation, raise a follow-up work item rather than widening this item.
- **Scope creep (medium likelihood, medium impact):** the change invites
  rebalancing asteroid counts, timers or accumulation caps. Mitigation:
  explicitly out of scope (Constraints); record any such idea as a
  `discovered-from:AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO` work item.
- **Gym/equivalence guard (low likelihood, medium impact):**
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` guards against duplicate gameplay bodies.
  Mitigation: keep the split code in the shared `asteroidSplit` helper; change
  only the `PlayScene` wave-accounting call site.
- **Boss-entry ambiguity (low likelihood, medium impact):** the assumption that
  carried-over asteroids are still cleared on boss entry is recorded and the
  open question is surfaced to the producer.
- **Regression in wave transitions (low likelihood, high impact):** removing
  dynamic registration could let a wave clear before a still-spawning enemy
  ship is released. Mitigation: enemy ships are all spawned synchronously in
  `spawnWave()`; only asteroids are scheduled, and they no longer gate the
  wave. Covered by AC1/AC7 tests.

## Assumptions (recorded, non-blocking)

- **Boss entry:** "between waves and levels" is taken to exclude the final boss
  transition; `_clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry` stays, consistent with GDD §4.1 E6
  ("boss encounter spawns no asteroids").
- **Accumulation:** because asteroids now persist and new ones spawn each wave,
  the field can grow over a run; this is the intended classic-Asteroids
  behaviour and no cap is introduced in this item.
- **Gyms:** no gym parity change is required because the wave model is
  PlayScene-only.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available (auto-dispatched intake), so no questions
were put to a human. The decisions above are supported by repository research:

- Q: "Does anything else depend on asteroids gating the wave?" — Research:
  `grep` of `registerDynamicSpawn` shows production use only in
  `PlayScene._spawnScheduledAsteroid` and `PlayScene._splitAsteroid`; other
  references are tests. `WaveManager` is used only by `PlayScene` (plus boss
  minion planning). Source: `src/`.
- Q: "What currently clears asteroids at the boss?" — Answer (research):
  `PlayScene._clearAsteroidsOnBossEntry()` (AH-0MUCG5TIU000VPVO), called from
  `_onTransitionComplete()` when `bossActive`. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Q: "Do minerals already persist between waves?" — Answer (research):
  `spawnWave()`/`_startTransition()` do not touch `this.minerals`; minerals are
  cleared only in `resetRunState()`/`teardownRunState()`. Source:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- Q: "Which tests assert the old rule?" — Answer (research):
  `PlayScene.test.ts` (AC3/AC6 asteroid-accounting suite,
  `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5`) and `WaveManager.test.ts` dynamic-spawn tests.
  Source: `src/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (for producer, non-blocking):** Should carried-over asteroids
also be cleared on boss entry, or should they persist into the boss encounter?
This brief assumes they are cleared (no behaviour change); confirm or correct if
the intent is full persistence.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB** – Gym asteroids do not drop minerals — share the mineral kill-drop code with the game (completed)
- **AH-0MUDY2R4S009F0JI** – Wire PlayScene lose-life path (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: asteroids, cleared, complete, completed, enemy (+8 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: asteroids, cleared, complete, enemy, levels (+7 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: asteroids, cleared, enemy, levels, minerals (+5 more)

## Summary

Add the pure, engine-agnostic danger-detection helper that decides when the player is "in danger" (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8). Per producer answers Q1 and Q5, danger is the **combined** count of hostile bodies and hostile bullets whose centre lies within `DANGER_RADIUS = 2 × SHIP_SIZE` (40 px) of the ship, and the player is in danger when that count is `>= DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD = 3`. This item is **test-first**: write the failing unit tests before implementing the helper.

## Why

Phase Shift becomes an automatic, reactive defensive tool; it needs a single, correct, unit-testable proximity judgement shared by every combat scene. Without it the auto-trigger has no input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1.1 — `src/core/constants.ts` exports `DANGER_RADIUS` (= `2 * SHIP_SIZE`, i.e. 40 with `SHIP_SIZE = 20`) and `DANGER_THREAT_THRESHOLD` (= 3); both are used by the helper (no duplicated literals).
- [ ] AC1.2 — A pure helper (e.g. `countThreatsInRange(ship, bodies, bullets)` and `isInDanger(...)`) lives in `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with **no Phaser import**.
- [ ] AC1.3 — Counting is by **centre-to-centre** distance from the ship; a threat exactly on the radius boundary (distance == `DANGER_RADIUS`) counts as inside.
- [ ] AC1.4 — Boundary tests: exactly 3 combined threats → in danger; 2 → not in danger; a threat just inside the radius counts and one just outside does not.
- [ ] AC1.5 — Enemy bodies (asteroids, boss, boss minions and all enemy archetypes) and live enemy bullets count; player bullets and minerals do **not** count.
- [ ] AC1.6 — `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass; the new tests fail against the pre-change (absent-helper) implementation, demonstrating TDD.
- [ ] AC1.7 — JSDoc on the helper documents the 40 px / >= 3 rule and the producer decision (Q1/Q5).

- [ ] Traceability — parent AC1 (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8): [ ] **AC1 — Danger detection is measurable and correct.** A pure, unit-testable helper counts hostile entities + hostile bullets within `2 × SHIP_SIZE` of the ship and reports "in danger" when the combined count is ≥ 3. Boundary cases are covered: exactly 3 threats triggers; 2 threats do not; threats just inside the radius count and just outside do not; asteroids, boss/minions and all enemy bullet types count; player bullets and minerals do not.


## Minimal Implementation

- Add the two constants to `src/core/constants.ts`.
- Create `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` with a small, total, allocation-light API: `distanceSq`-based counting, accepting read-only `{x,y}` arrays so it is trivially testable and reusable from the scene.
- Add `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts` covering AC1.3–AC1.5.

**Key Files:**
- `src/core/constants.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None (foundational). Parent: AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8.

## Summary

Add the dedicated Phase Shift audio cue that plays on every activation (parent AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8). Per producer answer Q4: a rising sci-fi whoosh/chirp, synthesised procedurally with the Web Audio API, degrading to a safe no-op without an AudioContext so headless tests never break.

## Why

accounting are correct. Non-lethal hits consume the bullet with no destruction

`CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` calls `enemy.takeDamage?.()` but
**discards its result** and never runs `onEnemyDestroyed`/destruction audio for
a multi-hit entity that dies. The `takeDamage(): number | void` seam exists
(`CombatCoreScene.CombatEnemyEntity`, `GymFormationScene.FormationSceneEntity`)

Second-review fix — root cause and approach.

Root cause reproduced with a scratch harness: sequencer() picked exactly one candidate group per wave, and a single group's enemyDifficulty score saturates around 33 (e.g. phaser×12). Every target ≥40 therefore produced the identical phaser×12 wave with a large error — exactly the 'repeat the phaser with shooting' and 'why actual/error' observations.

Fix (assumption documented): the gym cannot improve its own output without changing the shared sequencer, so difficultySequencer.ts was extended (originally listed read-only) to compose a wave from multiple candidate groups when one group cannot reach the target. Behaviour is backward compatible: a single group is still used whenever it already meets the target, so the game's calibrated CSV curve (targets ≤32) is byte-for-byte unchanged (verified with a scratch run). New options allowMultipleGroups (default true) and maxGroupsPerWave (default 5) were added. The gym passes tolerance 3 for accuracy.

The preview table now shows WAVE / TARGET / COMPOSITION / SHOOTING (the redundant ACTUAL and ERROR columns the producer questioned are gone); actualDifficulty remains on the model so tests can assert target matching. High targets now yield distinct multi-group compositions (e.g. phaser×12 + scout×18) instead of a repeated saturated archetype.
